note: Lines of the 0.7.0 standards changed on purpose during the 1.0.0 migration, each with its reason. The line-conservation check allows exactly these and nothing else. Heading lines that only gained a {#id} are not listed.

lines.before: 3. **One home per rule.** A rule lives in this file only. Memory, notes, briefs and tracking files hold a pointer (`-> _Working Standards.md "Section"`), never a restated copy.
lines.after: 3. **One home per rule.** A rule lives in this file only. Memory, notes, briefs and tracking files hold a pointer (`-> rule:<id>`, the fixed ID after the rule's heading), never a restated copy.
lines.why: The pointer form changed to the rule ID; the old form is what the link check now refuses.
